correctness.rationale: Telescoping yields ||W^k x||_p^p=sum_(j>k)|x_j|^p (j/(j-k))^beta (L(j)/L(j-k))^p. Potter bounds imply bounded weights for positive locally bounded slowly varying L; local uniform slow variation gives finite B_L. If C_L=sup_(j>=s) L(j)/L(s)<infinity, for any hit-time set E of m indices in [0,N) the sharp finite-column inequality sum_(k in E,k<j)(j/(j-k))^beta<=N^beta m^(1-beta)/(1-beta) gives uniform weak-q0 where beta=alpha p, q0=1/alpha. Converse uses x=e_j, N=j and s+1 consecutive residual indices in [s,2s], yielding C_L<=B_L max(1,2^alpha W_q0). Strong q<q0 follows Potter with q(alpha+epsilon)<1, Jensen for q>=p and monotonicity for q<p. At q0, the harmonic weighted ratio sum_(s<=j) s^-1(L(j)/L(s))^q0 diverges by every terminal multiplicative block and slow variation; at q>q0 the one large iterate suffices. The genuine nonmonotone slow-variation class is included; sample L(j)=log(e+j)^gamma has weak endpoint iff gamma<=0. Independent bounded finite-k inequality checks and source numeric_checker.py inspect complement, not replace, all-j arguments.
